theme: University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)
queries_run: gh search repos "upgo mcgill short term rental"
gh search repos "short-term rental dataset city"
gh search repos "urban planning airbnb research"
WebFetch raw READMEs: UPGo-McGill/strr, rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse, rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations, GarysCorner/NewORleansSTR, dolmios/airindex-2022

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE/R/) 'Tools for Analysis of Short-Term Rental Data' from McGill's Urban Politics and Governance (UPGo) lab (David Wachsmuth's group). Functions clean/process raw AirDNA property- and daily-level files, flag commercial/multi-listing operators, and detect 'ghost hotel' clusters of private-room listings. No data files committed (works on AirDNA exports the lab licenses separately); 5 stars, last updated 25 Aug 2025.
candidates.why_useful: This is the flagship UPGo (McGill) STR-research toolkit — the exact 'academic STR lab' the theme targets. The methodology (ghost-hotel detection, commercial-operator flags) could be re-applied to our own Inside Airbnb panel even though the underlying AirDNA feed is paid; also a pointer to the wider UPGo-McGill GitHub org (29 repos, see notes).
candidates.geography: Canada + multi-city (BC, Quebec, Halifax, LA, Charlottetown, Caribbean per org repos)
candidates.size_hint: small R package, no committed data

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/canada-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis code for 'Combs et al. 2019' — the peer-reviewed UPGo paper on Airbnb activity across Canadian cities. Repo holds R analysis scripts, not raw AirDNA data (licensed source); part of the same UPGo-McGill org as strr.
candidates.why_useful: Academic replication package for a published Airbnb-supply study; useful for methodology/benchmarks on Canadian STR growth even without the underlying proprietary data.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/bc-report-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: UPGo's 2024 British Columbia STR report build (R/ scripts, output/ folder). Checked output/: only 7 PNG figures (figure_2_1..3_3) are committed — no CSVs. Companion repos bc-report-2022 and bc-report-2023-summer exist in the same org for prior BC report vintages, same pattern (code + figures, no raw data).
candidates.why_useful: Point-in-time provincial STR supply/growth report (BC has had aggressive 2024 STR legislation); figures alone give visual time series but no machine-readable numbers were found committed.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/citq-rapport-2024
candidates.what_it_holds: UPGo's 2024 report build for CITQ (Corporation de l'industrie touristique du Québec — the Quebec STR licensing/registration body). Root contains only R/ scripts, LICENSE, .gitignore; no committed data files found at the top level.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms UPGo actively works with Quebec's CITQ STR registration data (a regulatory registry gap-relevant to item 12); code shows how to process CITQ data even though no dataset is committed here — worth pulling the underlying CITQ open registry directly rather than via this repo.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/ghost
candidates.what_it_holds: Small R function/package implementing UPGo's method for identifying 'ghost hotel' clusters (illegal multi-unit operations disguised as private-room listings) from STR listing data.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete, published algorithm for flagging commercial/illegal operators in an Inside Airbnb-style panel — could be run against our own 13-city or 120-market Inside Airbnb cohort to build a professional-host / supply-quality signal.

candidates.name: rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-warehouse project ('investigating the impact of Airbnb short-term rentals on world cities') that pulls Inside Airbnb listings (2015-2020, described as 'over 35 million records' across multiple world cities), plus Kaggle 'World Cities Population and Location' and Kaggle 'Cost of Living Indices' (Numbeo). Python extract.py/load.py load into Snowflake, transformed via dbt, visualized in Metabase. No static files committed — it is a live ETL pipeline over Inside Airbnb's history, not a repo of CSVs. 15 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #1: this pipeline claims to reach back to Inside Airbnb data from 2015-2020, i.e. years now off the official CDN (which keeps ~1 year). If the extract.py logic or any cached intermediate output can be recovered, it could backfill our pre-2023 Inside Airbnb gap across many cities, not just the ones we hold.
candidates.size_hint: "over 35 million records" (pipeline claim, not verified as committed)

candidates.name: rochiecuevas/shared_accommodations
candidates.what_it_holds: San Francisco STR/housing study with four committed CSVs: hotel_dailyrates.csv / hotel_monthlyrate.csv / hotel_yrrate.csv (SF hotel rates, Jul 2004-May 2018, source: SF City Performance Scorecards), yearly_rent.csv (Zillow long-term rent, Nov 2010-Sep 2018), and airbnbdataanalysis.csv (Inside Airbnb-derived, May 2015-Dec 2017). Home-price data (DataSF, 2007-2016) is referenced but not committed (file-size limit). 10 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Small but genuinely historical, committed Inside Airbnb-derived series for San Francisco spanning May 2015-Dec 2017 — years pre-dating our 13-city panel (Dec 2022+) and off the current CDN. Also a free SF hotel-rate time series back to 2004 (peer/lodging benchmark) and a Zillow SF rent series (housing gap #13).

candidates.name: GarysCorner/NewORleansSTR
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook (STRMaps.ipynb) that pulls New Orleans's 'Short-Term Rental Licenses' dataset from the city's open-data portal (data.nola.gov) and renders it as an interactive folium/Leaflet map of active STR license status. No historical snapshots committed — reads the live current portal export. 3 stars, updated 5 Aug 2026 (active).
candidates.why_useful: New Orleans is not in our current municipal-registry list (Austin, Barcelona, Maui, NYC, California TOT cities); this notebook is a working, recently-updated method for pulling that city's STR license registry directly from its Socrata-style open-data portal — cheap to adapt into our own point-in-time puller.
candidates.size_hint: notebook + generated HTML map, no bulk data file
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Municipal STR registries panel (Austin/Barcelona/Maui/NYC/California) — adds a new city, not a duplicate

candidates.name: dolmios/airindex-2022
candidates.what_it_holds: Archived (read-only since 31 May 2024) landing page for 'AirIndex', described only as 'a project testing techniques for aggregating and providing open short-term rental data from Airbnb' (WIP). Next.js/React/Supabase landing page; no cities, sources, or committed datasets documented in the repo itself; live site would be airindex.vercel.app (not verified reachable).
candidates.why_useful: Concept-stage aggregator for open STR data — flagged for completeness only; archived and undocumented, likely dead. Worth a 5-minute check of the live Vercel URL if someone wants to rule it out definitively.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill (org, 29 repos)
candidates.what_it_holds: Full GitHub org for McGill's Urban Politics and Governance lab (David Wachsmuth), the academic group most associated with independent Airbnb-supply research in Canada. Beyond the repos listed individually above, it holds: halifax-analysis, la-analysis/la-report-2021, charlottetown-analysis, herongate (Ottawa displacement study), cmhc-eviction-2022/2023, cmhc-transitions-2024, cmhc-rent-2023, cmhcr (near-empty CMHC data-import stub — checked, no data-raw/ folder), commercial-operators, deceptive_str_operations, community_resistance, illegal, image-recognition (listing-photo classification), covid-mapping. Pattern across every repo checked: R/Python analysis code only, built on AirDNA data the lab licenses privately — no raw STR CSVs committed anywhere in the org.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms UPGo is a real, active (some repos updated 2025-2026) academic STR-research lab exactly matching the theme brief, but their underlying data (AirDNA) is licensed, not open, so the org's value to us is methodology and report structure (ghost-hotel detection, commercial-operator flags, CMHC housing-transition linkage) rather than a data source. Individually flagged repos above are the highest-signal subset; the rest are lower-value variants of the same code pattern.
candidates.geography: Canada (multi-city: BC, Quebec, Halifax, Charlottetown, Ottawa, LA)

notes: gh search repos with multi-word AND-style queries (e.g. "upgo mcgill short term rental", "airbnb regulation dataset") returned empty results even though matching repos exist (confirmed by directly querying the UPGo-McGill org via gh api) — GitHub's repo search appears to require closer literal matches than code search; broader single/double-word queries ("airbnb", "short-term rental") worked. Recommend future scouts on this theme go straight to `gh api users/<org>/repos` for known labs (UPGo-McGill, MIT Real Estate Innovation Lab, university GIS/urban-informatics labs) rather than relying on repo-search keyword matching. WebSearch tool was unavailable for the back half of this run (session search-budget exhausted by other concurrent scouts), which cut off the city-planning-department and 'historical Inside Airbnb mirror' web searches I had queued — a follow-up scout with WebSearch budget available should retry those two queries: (1) site:github.com short-term rental registration dataset city planning department, (2) "inside airbnb" archive github historical dumps mirror 2015-2018. No repo found with a genuinely large, freely-licensed, multi-year committed STR panel from a university/municipal source beyond what CONTEXT.md already lists as held; the two closest (rsanjabi warehouse, rochiecuevas shared_accommodations) are worth a maintainer follow-up specifically for their pre-2023 Inside Airbnb coverage.
